# BtechPort and the BattleTech Construction Kit

The editor and desktop launcher are named **BattleTech Construction Kit**. They
create and edit game packages for the BtechPort player, including maps, events,
artwork and shared Unit and Construction Libraries.

An independent **C11 / SDL2** recreation of **BattleTech: The Crescent Hawk's
Inception** (1988), targeting the DOS **1.03** release.

This project uses **AI-assisted reverse engineering and development**, including
**OpenAI Sol 6.1 and Astra**, with human direction, gameplay reports and review.
AI helps investigate the original executable, interpret observations, implement
the port and build verification tools. AI-generated explanations are checked
against original data and executable behavior; they are not themselves evidence
of fidelity. See [research methods and AI use](docs/AI_AND_PROVENANCE.md).

**The implementation does not use the original game's source code.** It is
independently written from reverse-engineering research, original game data and
observations of the DOS executable. The substantial contributions of other
researchers are credited below.

**Original game assets are not included.** Everyone running the port must supply
the original DOS game files, including `BTECH.EXE`. Local extraction creates
ignored caches from those files; it does not download the game.

## Start the application

**Linux:** double-click `BtechPort.desktop` if present, or run `./BtechPort` once
and choose **Create launch shortcut**. **Windows:** double-click `BtechPort.cmd`
or `BtechPort.pyw` with Python/Tk installed.

The launch window provides **New game**, **Continue quicksave**, **Open editor**,
**Unit Library** and **New project**. Select Original, Updated, a demo or your own
project. **Build application** builds the local executables; **Player setup**
sets the original files if needed. The independent demos run without them.
See the [launcher and Unit Library guide](docs/UNIT_LIBRARY_AND_LAUNCHER.md).

The Construction Kit now includes service-building templates, a connected event
graph and quest journal, saved playtest checkpoints, building stamps, layered
pixel editing, generated jigsaw worlds, named animation actions and individual
infantry sprites. **Project** provides asset reports and explicit save migration.
**Play options → Checkpoints and trace** can verify later missions from a saved
point, with exact-content checks and saved RNG; see [saved journeys](docs/SAVED_JOURNEYS.md).
See the [five milestones](docs/EDITOR_COMPLETION_MILESTONES.md) and
[distribution guide](docs/CONSTRUCTION_KIT_DELIVERY.md). A packaged Linux kit
starts with `ConstructionKit` and includes Python/Tk/Pillow/SDL; a Windows kit
starts with `ConstructionKit.cmd` and can use an installed or supplied Python runtime.
Both packages include a console authoring launcher: `Author` on Linux and
`Author.cmd` on Windows. It exposes the same JSON interface used by external
AI authors, without requiring a model or network connection.

The editor now uses a single tabbed workspace with an explorer, Inspector,
Problems/output, direct unit-to-sprite and entrance-to-event navigation, shared
Undo/Redo and private recovery drafts. Project and library saves have explicit
separate scopes. Validation, imports, exports and playtest preparation run in the
background; Play/Stop manages an isolated test game. See the
[workspace guide](docs/EDITOR_WORKSPACE.md), [implementation stages](docs/EDITOR_USABILITY_PLAN.md)
and [verification results](docs/TESTING.md#editor-workspace-ui5--2026-10-18).
Native Windows editor interaction remains unverified.

Map authoring now includes **Building, Wall and Road designers**, a reusable
**Pattern Library**, terrain cut/copy/paste and tile editing directly from
construction/jigsaw previews. The tile chooser can clone an entire sheet into
editable project tiles. New worlds default to the original **1024 × 1024** size.
Open **Construction tools** in the explorer or use **Project**; see the
[map construction guide](docs/M5_WORLD_ART_EDITOR.md#buildings-walls-and-roads).

**Worlds / planets** now supports drawing imported CHI terrain with actual
**TINYLAND** graphics, placing jigsaws and painting individual tiles. Switch
to **Detailed tiles** for close editing; right-click to edit artwork against
its neighbours. Original jigsaw previews resolve their terrain level and
orientation correctly. See [world painting and jigsaws](docs/WORLD_TERRAIN_EDITING.md).

**Project → Construction Library** shares tiles, building, wall and road definitions
and saved patterns between games, with their animation frames, editing
layers and source credits. Designers and the project Pattern Library provide
**Save to library**; **Import and edit** opens a shared copy in another game.
**Edit in library** opens an independent workshop: edit the shared definition
or its pixels, draw on a persistent test canvas and use **Play** to try it.
Saving there updates the library; importing into a game remains explicit.
AI authors can search and import the same designs before drawing.
See the [Construction Library guide](docs/CONSTRUCTION_LIBRARY.md).

Construction designers show complete part coverage, including all four road
T-junction orientations and right-angle turns. The Road designer shows **Turn
N/E, E/S, S/W, W/N** and **T North / East / South / West** previews; right-click
one to choose, clone or edit its tile with the
surrounding road tiles visible. Walls default to zero stories (top tiles only).
Event graph boxes show editable descriptions; **Description** changes an author
note without changing game dialogue. Last Beacon includes descriptions for all
54 events. Click table headings for ascending, descending, then original order;
type the start of a dropdown item to select or complete it.

The shared **Unit Library** currently offers **82 blueprints: 66 mechs, ten
vehicles and six infantry templates**, including [25 additional classic
mechs](content/catalogues/mechs/README.md). Mechs use Locust or red Stinger
animations according to leg type; infantry uses the original animations.
Edit designs and sprites inside the library, import selected
designs into games, or export game designs back as updates/variants. Dependencies,
source credits, conflict handling and Undo/Redo accompany imports.

## Status

The game is playable from training through the campaign ending. Exploration,
shops and services, recruitment, mixed infantry/mech combat, the Star League
cache and six save slots are implemented. Original graphics, animations, text
and PC-speaker programs are read from the supplied files.

Fidelity work continues. Original routine comparisons and repeatable gameplay
routes verify specific behavior; they do not establish complete parity. Combat
presentation/timing, wider encounter behavior, some transitions and physical
speaker response still have limits. See [project status](docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md)
and the [weapon/fire presentation audit](docs/WEAPON_PRESENTATION.md) for the
latest evidence. The [mech movement and LRM AI analysis](docs/MECH_MOVEMENT_AND_LRM_AI.md)
records the verified movement calculations and implemented Updated combat rules.

Original/Legacy saves retain v44; Enhanced combat and its settings use v45.
Held broker category menus use v46 in Updated's existing save envelope.
Older saves remain loadable, including held combat effects.
Rebuilding prepares the updated local combat cache from your original files.

The proposed path to more mechs, custom game packages, BLD/Lua scripting and a
Windows/Linux editor is recorded in the
[engine and editor plan](docs/ENGINE_AND_EDITOR_PLAN.md).

The [editable CHI campaign plan](docs/CHI_EDITABLE_CAMPAIGNS_PLAN.md) specifies
five milestones for importing separate Original and Updated campaigns
from a user's original files. It covers editable maps/scripts/services, isolated
saves and keeping original-derived content out of repository and release assets.
Choose **Import CHI** in the launcher to create both local
projects. **Project → CHI maps and world** edits native maps, town placements,
generator inputs, entrances and jigsaws; **CHI resources** edits presentation
art/animation and supported audio settings; **CHI campaign** edits native text.
**Project → CHI scripts** provides C4.1's labelled BLD dialogue/control-flow
editing and lossless compiler. **CHI services** exposes C4.2's prices,
inventories, repair/healing/recruitment settings and named native actions, with
linked price text and saved continuations. **CHI missions and campaign** exposes
training opponents/outcomes, invasion, encounters, arena, cache and initial
state settings. See [import instructions](docs/CHI_IMPORT.md),
[BLD authoring](docs/BLD_AUTHORING.md), [services](docs/CHI_SERVICE_AUTHORING.md)
and [missions](docs/CHI_MISSION_AUTHORING.md). **CHI script coverage** now shows
source-linked BLD execution from Play traces; see [native coverage](docs/CHI_NATIVE_COVERAGE.md).
Older imports expose **Local maps (enable editing)** in the project tree.
**CHI quests** adds optional dialogue, battles and rewards through native
doorways or BLD calls, with saved returns and supported native service adapters.
Use **Add example quest** to try it; see [quest authoring](docs/CHI_QUEST_AUTHORING.md).
**Project → CHI reconstruction recipes** shares supported campaign edits as
changes and local-original references. See [sharing/reconstruction](docs/CHI_RECONSTRUCTION.md)
and [campaign acceptance and platform limits](docs/CHI_ACCEPTANCE.md). C4.5 and
C5 implementation are verified for the declared Linux/Wine scope. The
[independent Astra audit](docs/CHI_ASTRA_AUDIT.md) found and fixed recipe,
save-discovery and verification issues. The
[refreshed application packages](docs/DELIVERY_REFRESH_20261024.md) contain these
fixes and pass packaged Linux and Windows/Wine checks. Native Windows Tk
verification remains pending.
A separate [Enhanced-only campaign route](docs/CHI_ENHANCED_ACCEPTANCE.md) now
reaches the ending with default Enhanced rules throughout, matching the built-in
Updated game on Linux and Windows/Wine, including saved continuations.
The launcher has **Saved games...** and the editor has **Play → Saved games**:
six slots, dates, revisions, backups, exact-revision Continue and recovery into
empty slots. Project revisions are retained before play so later editing does
not orphan their saves. Editor Play saves persist between launches. See
[saved games and recovery](docs/EDITOR_SAVE_GAMES.md) before editing a campaign
you want to keep playing with existing saves.
The [essential-character death popup](docs/GAME_OVER_PRESENTATION.md) now uses
the original text and wrapping; older imported campaigns have an explicit
update utility that preserves their progress.

[World-route checks](docs/WORLD_ROUTE_VERIFICATION.md) exercise whole-party
travel between towns and planets, discovery and save/reload, with navigable
editor diagnostics. The independent World Survey fixture needs no original assets.

[AI authoring tools](docs/AI_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md) can inspect projects, search
assets, apply validated command batches, export labelled visual previews, check
mission navigation and run seeded gameplay suites through `python3 tools/author.py`.
The editor's **Project** menu has **Content catalogue**, **Check mission**,
**Changes and protection** and **Local authoring session**, alongside command-file
exchange. Review proposed maps/events, protect human edits, and accept changes
with shared Undo and revision checks. External authors can take snapshots of
the open editor and submit scoped proposals; review is the default.
[World reviews](docs/WORLD_REVIEW.md) add paired planet previews, town navigation
and protected terrain rectangles, including changes to shared jigsaws and art.
[Scenario selection](docs/SCENARIO_SELECTION.md) explains which regression cases
a proposal may affect. In **Changes → Checks**, choose a suite, review the reasons,
and run selected cases or the full suite against the retained candidate.
[Test suite authoring](docs/TEST_SUITE_AUTHORING.md) is available under **Play →
Test suites and coverage**. Create cases and route starters, edit steps and seeds,
import/export CLI suites, and navigate failures and observed event/branch coverage.
Try **Relay Contract (command-created)** in the launcher.
**Cairn Passage (defence / escort)** demonstrates timed defence, reinforcements,
friendly guards and a neutral Skulker convoy, with save/reload and loss routes.
Select it in `./BtechPort` to play or edit it. See the
[demo instructions](examples/cairn-passage/README.md) and
[combat authoring guide](docs/COMBAT_MISSIONS.md).

**Greybank Dispatch (campaign)** combines a depot/service loop, a choice of
Jenner assault or data recovery, timed defence and a vehicle escort. Play or
edit it in the launcher. To generate your own copy, check both branches and
launch it with your configured original resources:

```sh
python3 tools/author.py recipe build \
  --file examples/authoring/greybank/recipe.json \
  --output "work/My Greybank campaign" --check --play
```

The [recipe guide](docs/CAMPAIGN_RECIPES.md) covers parameters, recorded inputs,
diagnostics, source editing and delivery. Generation and gameplay work offline.

**Argent Recovery (regions / objectives)** demonstrates AI6a: named map regions,
typed counters, explicit objective states and compound extraction conditions,
with saved event continuations. The [mission reference](docs/MISSION_STATE.md)
documents the editor controls and lifecycle rules.
For a separate playable discovery/repair demonstration, run
`python3 tools/authoring_demo.py --output work/my-authoring-lab` after preparing
the original resources. It retains previews, exact commands and test reports
beside the new game. The [eight-milestone plan](docs/AI_AUTHORING_PLAN.md) records
the completed boundaries and proposed mission/campaign work. The full manual
editor remains central; generated games run without an AI service.

**Modular campaign sources** are available through **Project → Campaign sources
and build**. Create a separate source copy, edit it normally, and build a playable
package; maps, missions, definitions and dialogue live in separate files.
`python3 tools/author.py source convert PROJECT --output NEW_SOURCE_DIRECTORY`
provides the same workflow for automated authors. See the
[source/build guide](docs/CAMPAIGN_SOURCES.md), including save compatibility and
the reproducible two-planet Cairn example. Existing projects need no conversion.

**Larger campaigns:** the same panel's **Upgrade campaign limits** enables
64 local maps, 64 encounters, 1,024 events and 128 objectives/variables.
This optional v3 format requires runtime 0.2.0 and a new campaign; retain the
old package for its existing saves. AI authors use `campaign.upgrade`.
See [limits and the reproducible 20-contract fixture](docs/CAMPAIGN_CAPACITY.md).

The [shared authoring format and project loader](docs/M5_AUTHORING_PROJECTS.md)
now support editable CHI-dependent projects, up to 256 mech definitions, custom
weapon statistics, explicit portrait assets and separate package-bound saves.
Use `btp-project export` to make an editable copy of Updated, or start with the
[Workshop example](examples/project-demo/README.md). The
[project guide](docs/M5_AUTHORING_PROJECTS.md#create-validate-and-play) gives
export, validation and play commands for both platforms. Original and Updated
remain available as before. [Authored maps and events](docs/M5_MAPS_EVENTS_EDITOR.md)
now support entrances, overlays, shop stock, recruitment, transfers, battles and
saved continuations. Try [Frontier Depot](examples/adventure-demo/README.md).
For a BattleTech adventure, try **[BattleTech: Last Beacon](examples/battletech-demo/README.md)**:
three maps, nine established mech variants and ten vehicles, a Phoenix Hawk/Trebuchet starting
team, two mercenary contracts, a broker, recruitment and two endings. It uses
your supplied CHI graphics/sound and defaults to Enhanced combat:

```sh
sh scripts/play-battletech-demo.sh
python3 tools/game_editor.py examples/battletech-demo
```

See [verification and the next editor milestones](docs/BATTLETECH_DEMO.md).
The [world and graphics editor guide](docs/M5_WORLD_ART_EDITOR.md) covers jigsaws,
multiple planets, city placement, the full tile browser and pixel/animation editing.
Select a tile and **Edit pixels** to draw it; **Clone**, **Flip X/Y**, rotations,
nudging, fill, transparency and undo/redo are available. Roster selections show
animated sprites; right-click to edit or choose one. Mechs, vehicles, weapons
and heat-sink/jump-jet equipment can be created through **New definition**.

Try the new **[Vehicle proving ground](examples/vehicle-lab/README.md)** with
Patton, Rommel, Pegasus, Skulker, Drillson, Galleon, Scorpion, Vedette and the two
missile carriers. It has two planets, a depot and a live battle, with original
editable art and no requirement for CHI files:

```sh
./build/btech-port --project examples/vehicle-lab --save-file work/vehicle-lab.btp
python3 tools/game_editor.py examples/vehicle-lab
```

Use **New project** to work on a copy. **Unit Library → Vehicles → Import into game**
adds selected presets to an authored project. [Vehicle rules and source notes](content/catalogues/vehicles/README.md)
identify approximations; these presets do not replace the original campaign roster.

For clear editor text on Linux, use the distribution's Python with `python3-tk`
and `python3-pil`. The launcher prefers that interpreter when Conda's minimal Tk
is active and the system Tk is available. Windows uses normal Python/Tk.
The [game editor and independent demo](docs/M5_INDEPENDENT_GAME_EDITOR.md)
now add map painting, overlays, entrances/NPCs, encounters, event/choice forms,
roster editing, shared validation, undo/redo, export and Play here:

```sh
./build/btech-port --project examples/beacon-demo --save-file work/beacon-game.btp
python3 tools/game_editor.py examples/beacon-demo
```

[Visual editing](docs/EDITOR_GRAPHICS_AND_DRAGGING.md) now includes real map
graphics, a thumbnail palette, a full tile-sheet picker and marker dragging,
with a cleaner desktop layout. CHI projects use the original game folder from
**Player setup**; **Reload graphics** refreshes the previews.

[Last Beacon](examples/beacon-demo/README.md) is a complete tiny quest with its
own graphics, font, text, sound and a bounded Lua event. It requires **no original
files or caches**. Use New project in the editor to make your own copy. The guide
includes a build without original files and Windows setup. The old roster-editor
launcher remains supported, including `work/editor-ready` for the exported
31-mech CHI roster. Richer script authoring, packaging and construction rules
remain future work; the pixel, frame and world tools described above are usable now.

An ordinary launch first asks **Original BTECH CHI** or **Updated BTECH CHI**,
before the Westwood/Infocom logo. Original is the default. Use arrows and
Enter/Space, or press 1/2. Restart and choose Original whenever you want the
original lineup. `--edition original` or `--edition updated` skips the selector.

Updated adds **31 models**, from the UrbanMech to the 100-ton Atlas, including
Zeus, both Crusader variants, Phoenix Hawk, Shadow Hawk, Dragon, Grasshopper,
Highlander, Rifleman, Stalker, Jenner, Ostsol, Javelin, Cicada, Clint,
Hermes II, Whitworth and Ostroc.
In Starport, enter the central doorway of the unused three-door building
northeast of Mech-It Lube (local position 54,50, approached from the south).
The **'Mech Broker** has a newly generated 1980s anime-style salesman portrait,
a building description and compact **Buy**, **Sell** and **Leave** choices.
Choose **Buy a 'Mech → Light, Medium, Heavy or Assault**. Each class lists
its stock by tonnage, then name. **Up/Down scrolls**; Enter or Space selects.
Back/Backspace returns one menu level. The
[artwork guide](content/updated/art/README.md) includes masters, prompts and
PNG-to-ANM conversion instructions. Updated also adds portraits to the Training
Center, lounge, prison, inventor's hut, cinema, hospital, ComStar, clothes shop,
Video Hut and mayor's house. These
static illustrations preserve the buildings' scripts and original cutscenes.
New models cost 10,000–70,000 C-bills and
are parked outside for crew assignment when you leave through the garage.
The fleet has **four owned bays**. The counter shows occupancy; a fifth purchase
takes no money. Sell an original or added mech to free a bay, retaining its
crew. Offers include installed equipment and fall with damage. Added models
can also appear in eligible outdoor encounters and be salvaged under the
existing rules.
See [roster details and sources](content/updated/README.md).

New Updated games use **Enhanced combat**: mechs choose positions and volleys
from their usable weapons, ammunition and heat. LRM carriers can retreat and
wait for a better shot while moving. LRMs receive an accuracy penalty within
six adapted range units; close shots remain possible, and the targeting panel
shows the penalty. These authored rules apply equally to player and enemy
attacks. The planner runs locally as deterministic C code.

**Existing saves keep Legacy combat**, including Original saves imported into
Updated. Outside a battle, press **Space → Change game settings → Combat rules**
and select **Enhanced** to enable it, or **Legacy** to restore the original rules
and planning. This preserves your party, mechs and progress. Original mode
always retains Legacy combat. See [rules, limits and test results](docs/MECH_MOVEMENT_AND_LRM_AI.md).

Inspection bars scale larger armor/structure totals into the original diagram.
A temporary follower workaround regroups active units after building/battle
exits and closing menus, and recovers units more than six tiles from their
formation position. It applies to both editions and excludes parked/wrecked
mechs. The [implementation and removal TODO](port/core/party.c) distinguish it
from original behavior; the underlying routing still needs improvement.

Updated keeps six separate save slots, starting at
`work/player-save-updated.btp`; Original keeps `work/player-save.btp`.
`--load` recognizes the edition. To continue an existing original save as a
separate Updated campaign, use `--edition updated --load PATH`.
Existing three-, 17- and 23-model Updated saves load automatically with the expanded roster.
The loader verifies that all earlier definitions are unchanged before accepting
appended models. Editing/removing earlier definitions still requires their
matching roster. See [save behavior](docs/M5A_ROSTER_SLICE.md#starting-switching-and-saving).

## Build and run on Linux

You need a C11 compiler (GCC or Clang), CMake 3.16 or newer, Python 3 and SDL2
development files. On Debian, Ubuntu or Kubuntu, these can be installed with:

```sh
sudo apt install build-essential cmake python3 libsdl2-dev
```

1. Place the original DOS 1.03 game files directly in `Original DOS/` in this
   repository. Keep the original uppercase filenames. Use the complete game
   directory, including its executable, maps, scripts, graphics and animations.
   The supported executable is identified in [the file audit](docs/ORIGINAL_FILES.md).
2. From the repository root, build:

   ```sh
   ./scripts/build.sh
   ```

   This prepares the local resource caches in `work/` and builds the SDL2 game
   and headless tools in `build/`. It leaves the original files unchanged.
3. Run from the repository root:

   ```sh
   ./build/btech-port --data "Original DOS"
   ```

No DOS emulator, Godot, .NET or reference checkout is needed to build or play.
Python's standard library suffices for cache preparation. Optional research
and GUI verification tools have separate dependencies described in
[TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md).

For an incremental rebuild after editing C code:

```sh
cmake --build build -j4
```

If your game files are elsewhere, prepare the three caches with that same path
before configuring and building directly:

```sh
python3 tools/prepare_talk.py --data /path/to/game
python3 tools/prepare_combat.py --data /path/to/game
python3 tools/prepare_world.py --data /path/to/game
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build -j4
./build/btech-port --data /path/to/game
```

The convenience build script and most reference tests expect `Original DOS/`.
The native runtime also supports custom cache paths; see `--help`.

## Windows build and run

A Windows x86-64 executable can be cross-built on Linux with MinGW-w64 and the
[official SDL2 MinGW development archive](https://www.libsdl.org/release/SDL2-devel-2.32.4-mingw.tar.gz).
Install `gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64-posix` using your package manager, then extract the
SDL archive under `local-deps/windows/` and run:

```sh
./scripts/build-windows.sh
```

For SDL2 elsewhere, set `BTP_WINDOWS_SDL2` to its
`x86_64-w64-mingw32/lib/cmake/SDL2` directory. `BTP_WINDOWS_CC` can select a
particular MinGW compiler. The script prepares the same three resource caches
and creates `build-windows/btech-port.exe` with `SDL2.dll` beside it.

On Windows, retain that build directory, the `content` directory for Updated,
your `Original DOS` directory and the
three generated files `work/talk-data.bin`, `work/combat-data.bin` and
`work/world-data.bin` under a common directory. Open a terminal there and run:

```powershell
.\build-windows\btech-port.exe --data "Original DOS"
```

The executable and its input, saves and audio queue are tested under Wine on
Linux. Actual Windows drivers and physical audio hardware remain unverified.
See [Windows verification](docs/M4_PORTABILITY_SWEEP.md#5-windows-build-and-verification).

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move or select; hold perpendicular arrows to move diagonally |
| Numeric keypad | Move in eight directions; Num-Lock-off arrows work in menus |
| Enter or Space | Confirm a menu choice or advance dialogue |
| Space during exploration | Open the game menu |
| Escape or Backspace | Back out or decline; Escape does not quit |
| F4 | Toggle the explored overhead map |
| F5 / F9 | Save / load the selected slot |
| F3 | Toggle diagnostics |
| Ctrl + Shift + Escape | Quit |
| Hold Shift, then K, Y, R | Add 10,000 C-bills, including during the intro |

Amount fields accept digits, Backspace and Enter; Space does not submit a number.
Use the Space menu for walking step size, party inspection, equipment, map and
all six save slots. During combat, select a unit, give movement/weapon orders,
and use **Begin Fight** to resolve them. **Computer** assigns the selected unit
without starting a fight; use **Next Mech** to assign others. Space interrupts
automatic play at the end of the current wave and returns to the menu, retaining
the individual assignments. Giving manual movement or weapon orders returns
that unit to manual control.
Space also confirms manual combat commands, movement destinations, weapon and
target choices, and Yes/No prompts.

## Saves and useful options

Native saves default to `work/player-save.btp`; slots two through six add `-2`
through `-6` before `.btp`. They retain held menus and in-progress combat.
Use `--save-file PATH` to change the slot base filename.

```sh
./build/btech-port --load work/player-save.btp
./build/btech-port --mute
./build/btech-port --help
```

Original `GAME*` saves can also be imported:

```sh
./build/btech-port --load "Original DOS/GAME3"
```

All six supplied original saves have byte-for-byte import/export comparisons.
Export requires a previously imported original save and a supported outdoor
state; see [save compatibility](docs/M4_PROGRESS.md). Keep exported files outside
the original reference directory, for example `--export-original work/GAME3`.

## Verification and development

Run the fast headless suite after building:

```sh
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

For the broader historical verification workflow, use `./scripts/test.sh`.
GUI tests, sanitizer checks, deterministic replays and optional original-executable
oracles are documented in [TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md). Tests require your local
game files and generated caches. Native builds and tests do not need DOSBox;
original-game capture tools do.

| Directory | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `port/core/` | Deterministic game rules and serializable state |
| `port/data/` | Resource and save readers |
| `port/frontend/` | Rendering, SDL2 input/audio and headless entry points |
| `tools/`, `tests/` | Extraction, original comparisons and regression tests |
| `docs/` | Research, evidence, milestones and known gaps |
| `work/`, `build/` | Ignored local caches, captures, saves and build output |

`Original DOS/` and `UnBattletech/` are read-only reference directories, excluded
from this repository. Do not commit proprietary assets, extracted text, original
RAM dumps or screenshots. Findings use **VERIFIED**, **INFERRED**,
**APPROXIMATE** and **UNKNOWN** to make their limits explicit.

## License

BtechPort's independently authored code and documentation are licensed under the
**GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPL-3.0-only)**. See [LICENSE](LICENSE)
for the full terms. Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses.
The optional [Updated roster data](content/updated/README.md) adapts MegaMek
unit records and has a separate **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** data license. It is not
covered by the engine's GPL license.
The [newly generated building artwork](content/updated/art/README.md) is a separate
contribution under GPL-3.0-only to the extent copyright applies; its AI provenance
and generation prompts are recorded with the assets.

This license does not cover or grant rights to the original game executable,
artwork, music, text or other game assets. The original DOS installation and
extracted runtime caches must be supplied by the person running the port.
The public [Last Beacon baseline](examples/battletech-demo/README.md) uses
placeholders and a local reconstruction recipe for 20 CHI-derived tiles.
Original-derived working copies remain private; 17 historical edited variants
cannot be reproduced by the base-tile recipe. See
[asset handling](docs/CHI_IMPORT.md#original-derived-art-and-sharing).

## Acknowledgements

BtechPort builds on substantial reverse-engineering work by others. Their
research made this recreation possible and deserves explicit credit:

- **[UnBattletech](https://github.com/velteyn/UnBattletech), by Edoardo Barolo
  (`velteyn`) and its contributors, including Maximilien Noal.** Its file-format
  specifications, memory maps, story and engine research, annotated disassembly
  and decompiler output, and extraction tools supplied the main starting point
  for this port's research. We used its BLD round-trip converter for the initial
  audit and its documentation and assembly to locate original routines for
  further verification. UnBattletech is licensed under GPL-3.0.
- **The [Reko](https://github.com/uxmal/reko) and Spice86 contributors.** Their

  Its published EXEPACK header description informed this project's independently
  written unpacker and executable-format audit.

This port's independent C implementation and original-game validation extend
that research foundation. Detailed sources and verification limits are recorded
in the [research audit](docs/RESEARCH_AUDIT.md) and milestone evidence reports.

published by **Infocom**.

# AGS 2.x Decompilation

A matching decompilation project of Adventure Game Studio (AGS) 2.x. \
The goal is to decompile all publicly released AGS 2.x versions for software preservation and educational purposes.

This project focuses **only** on runtime engine and does **not** include editor components (`roomedit` for DOS and later `agsedit` for Windows).

The code in this repository is the result of reverse-engineering, source reconstruction and instruction matching processes. Source reconstruction is based on AC 1.14 [roommake](https://archive.org/details/rmakesrc) and AGS [legacy](https://github.com/adventuregamestudio/ags/tree/legacy) sources with main focus on producing source code as close to original as possible.

## Status

Version 2.00 is **complete** and demo game is fully playable. Next milestone would be 2.05 since it's the first version that can be tested against a "real" game: LassiQuest.

For more information refer to [STATUS](./STATUS.md).

## Comparing versions

As more information is gained over time, previously finished versions can be altered slightly. So do **NOT** rely on commit history to get differences between them. Use `git diff --no-index` on source directories instead.

For example, to compare versions 2.00 and 2.01 execute this from project root directory:
```sh
git diff --no-index ags200/src ags201/src
```

## Building

This project is using GNU `make` as its build system. Starting with AGS 2.03, it can be built for two targets: **DOS** (DJGPP) and **Windows** (MSVC).

**Before** you can build, you need to setup the DJGPP environment or a cross-compiler for targeting DOS, and the MSVC environment for targeting Windows. Instructions are provided in [BUILD](./docs/BUILD.MD) documentation.

The instructions below assume that you have the DJGPP and MSVC environments set up.

To build a specific AGS version, first navigate to its folder (e.g. `ags203`) and run `make prepare`:
```sh
cd ags203/ && make prepare
```
This will create necessary folder structure (run `make prepare` only once).

To build using DJGPP environment just invoke `make`:
```sh
make
```

For DJGPP cross-compilation, pass `DJGPP_DIR` variable pointing to cross-compiler root folder (e.g. `~/cross/4.9.4/djgpp`):
```sh
make DJGPP_DIR=~/cross/4.9.4/djgpp
```

For MSVC compilation, pass `MSVC_DIR` variable pointing to MSVC root folder (e.g. `~/cross/msvc/98`):
```sh
make MSVC_DIR=~/cross/msvc/98
```

For more information refer to [BUILD](./docs/BUILD.MD).

## Instruction matching

This process ensures that reconstructed source code, when compiled with a specific compiler version, produces identical to original binary assembly instructions. Matching is done against each function across all object files manually with the help of a simple diffing script.

Keep in mind this does **not** gurantee that output is byte-to-byte identical, since jump instructions may have different targets and global variables are placed at different addresses. Thus, a behavior matching process should follow this step to ensure identical behavior. This project doesn't have a goal of perfecly aligning data and compilation units.

Instruction matching should be done on **host** system since `diff_symbol.sh` script requires relatively modern versions of `bash` and `binutils`, you would also need `cat` (part of textutils), `grep`, `awk`, `diff` and `less` installed.

Make sure you've successfully compiled `ac.exe` (or `acwin.exe`) and `obj` directory contains object files.

Run following command to do matching of function `update_stuff` from `AC.O` compiled for DOS:
```sh
make diff OBJECT=AC.O SYMBOL=update_stuff
```

In some cases there might be more then one function with a similar name, you can specify symbol index to select one of them:
```sh
make diff OBJECT=AC.O SYMBOL=run_animation SYMBOL_INDEX=1
```

For Windows version pass `TOOLCHAIN=msvc` variable into `make`:
```sh
make diff TOOLCHAIN=msvc OBJECT=ac.obj SYMBOL=update_stuff
```

GNU `objdump` has issues disassembling Windows COFF files, so for Windows version `llvm-objdump` is used.

Refer to `orig/ac_symbols.txt` (or `orig/acwin_symbols.txt`) file for the list of all functions that can be matched. This list is obtained through reverse-engineering and exporting tagged functions from Ghidra. Symbols file contains virtual memory addreses (VMAs). To convert to file offset, subtract section VMA and add section file offset.

For information regarding instruction matching and GCC2 specific patterns refer to [GCC2_NOTES](./docs/GCC2_NOTES.md).

# Wasted Dreams HLE — run the Amiga CD game natively with SDL3

A small PC host that runs the **original, unmodified 68k executable** of
*Wasted Dreams* (Digital Dreams Entertainment, 1999, Amiga CD32/AGA CD-ROM)
on Windows, Linux and macOS.

It is not a general Amiga emulator and needs **no Kickstart ROM**:

- a 68020 interpreter runs the game code;
- the few AmigaOS calls the game makes (exec, dos, graphics, intuition,
  ciab.resource, input.device) are **trapped and implemented in C**
  ("high-level emulation", HLE);
- the parts of the AGA chipset the game drives directly (copper, bitplanes,
  sprites, blitter, Paula audio, CIAs) are modelled just enough;
- video, audio and input go through **SDL3**.

The game boots, plays its FMV intro, and is playable in one- or two-player
mode with keyboard, joystick emulation or real gamepads, at full speed.

> **No game data is included.** This package contains only the host's own
> source code. You need your own copy of the *Wasted Dreams* CD. The game,
> its executable, data, music, video and manual remain the property of their
> rights holders and must not be redistributed with this code.

---

## 1. Build

Requirements: a C11 compiler, CMake ≥ 3.16, and **SDL3** (≥ 3.2).

### Linux

```sh
# SDL3 from your distribution if available (e.g. Ubuntu 25.04+: libsdl3-dev),
# otherwise build it from source (https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL):
#   cmake -S SDL -B SDL/build -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$HOME/sdl3 && cmake --build SDL/build -j && cmake --install SDL/build
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$HOME/sdl3     # prefix only needed for a custom SDL3 install
cmake --build build -j
```

For windowed play on Linux, SDL3 must be built with your desktop's video and
audio backends (X11/Wayland + PulseAudio/PipeWire development packages
installed before configuring SDL3).

### macOS

```sh
brew install sdl3 cmake
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j
```

### Windows (Visual Studio 2022)

Download the official `SDL3-devel-<version>-VC.zip` from
<https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases>, unpack it, then:

```bat
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:\path\to\SDL3-<version>
cmake --build build --config Release
```

`SDL3.dll` is copied next to `wd_host.exe` automatically.

Fallback if you only have `SDL3.dll` and the SDL3 headers (no CMake package):
`-DWD_SDL3_DLL=C:\path\SDL3.dll -DWD_SDL3_INCLUDE=C:\path\SDL3\include`
(an import library is generated with `tools/make_msvc_implib.py`; needs Python 3).

The executable ends up in `build/bin/` (`build/bin/Release/` with Visual Studio).

---

## 2. Combine with the game

The host needs the files from the **root of the game CD** in one folder:

```
WASTED            <- the 68k executable (the one this host runs)
WDDATA/  WDSOUND/  WDVIDEO/
(ENGINE, WASTEDDREAMS, *.INFO, WDMANUAL/ are not needed but harmless)
```

Get them from your CD or your own disc image:

- **Windows:** double-click the `.iso` to mount it and copy the files, or
  `7z x WastedDreams.iso -oC:\Games\WastedDreams`.
- **Linux:** `7z x WastedDreams.iso -o~/games/wasted-dreams` or mount it
  (`sudo mount -o loop,ro WastedDreams.iso /mnt` and copy).
- **macOS:** `hdiutil attach WastedDreams.iso` and copy from the mounted volume.
- A `.bin/.cue` image with a single MODE1/2048 track is the same as an `.iso`.

File-name case does not matter (the host matches names case-insensitively on
Linux and macOS).

Run it from that folder, or point at it:

```sh
wd_host --dir /path/to/game            # like the CD's main icon: full story intro
wd_host --dir /path/to/game --args ""  # like the "ENGINE" script: short logos, straight into the game
```

Created in the game folder: `wd.ini` (input configuration, written on first
run), `_sys/S/` (the game's settings and save slots — the game saves to
`SYS:S/`), and `wd.log` in the current directory (diagnostics).

---

## 3. Playing

In the game's default setup player 1 (green) uses the joystick in port 2 and
player 2 (blue) the keyboard. Press **Esc** for the game menu: *options →
players* switches between 1 and 2 players (restarts the game), *controls*
chooses keyboard or joystick per player.

| Input | Amiga |
|---|---|
| Arrow keys, Shift / Return | keyboard player: move, action / fire |
| Numpad 8/2/4/6 (7/9/1/3 diagonals), Numpad 0 or 5 | joystick in port 2 |
| Gamepad 1 (stick or D-pad, A/B/right trigger = fire) | joystick in port 2 |
| Gamepad 2 | joystick in port 1 (replaces the mouse while connected) |
| Left Alt / pad 1 X or LB | hold: player 1 rucksack (left/right picks the active item) |
| Right Alt / pad 2 X or RB | hold: player 2 rucksack |
| Esc / pad Start or Back | game menu, skips intro clips |
| Mouse (click the window to capture, F12 releases) | Amiga mouse |
| F11 | screenshot to `shots/` |

Game basics (from the game's manual): actions (look, take, talk, use) appear
as an icon next to your player panel when available — press fire/Shift to do
them. Items are used by making them the *active* object in the rucksack
before approaching the place or person that needs them. Text stays on screen
until you press fire.

### Input configuration (`wd.ini`)

Created with commented defaults on first run; delete it to restore them.
`--config file.ini` selects another file. Problems are reported in `wd.log`.

```ini
[port2]                    ; Amiga joystick port 2
pad = 1                    ; 1st/2nd connected pad, 0 = none, or part of its name ("dualsense")
stick = left               ; left / right / none
dpad = yes
deadzone = 35              ; percent
fire = a, b, righttrigger  ; pad buttons pressing the joystick button
button.x = lalt            ; pad button -> Amiga key while held
button.start = esc
key.up = Keypad 8          ; PC keys acting as this joystick (also down/left/right/upleft/.../fire)

[port1]
mode = auto                ; auto | joystick | mouse
pad = 2

[keyboard]                 ; PC key = Amiga key (or none)
Left Ctrl = lalt
```

Pad buttons: `a b x y back guide start leftstick rightstick leftshoulder
rightshoulder dpup dpdown dpleft dpright lefttrigger righttrigger` (a = bottom
face button). PC keys use SDL key names (`A`, `Space`, `Left Ctrl`, `Keypad 8`).
Amiga keys: `esc return enter space bs tab del help up down left right lshift
rshift ctrl lalt ralt lamiga ramiga f1`–`f10 kp0`–`kp9`, a PC key name, or a raw
code like `$45`.

---

# gielda
12-14 year old me project in Turbo Pascal, reverse engineered by Fable from executable with debugging symbols.


Note: this is terrible code just like you'd expect from driven non-educated 12-14 year old.


In 1998/99, there was very limited access to good CS books in Poland, limited internet, no stack overflow etc...

# Commentary from Claude Fable

## Initial investigation

Done — and this went far better than a typical lost-source recovery, because you compiled with debug info enabled. The EXE carries a full Turbo Debugger symbol table: 854 original identifier names, 664 symbols, and 2,107 line-number records.

Highlights of what came back:

Project layout — program gielda (G.PAS, ~1,582 lines, saved 1999‑02‑11 19:11) + three units: data1 (DATA1.PAS, the price engine — dated March 1997, two years older than the rest), data2 (DATA2.PAS, the F4 prognosis screens, ~896 lines), and import (EGAVGA BGI driver + SANS font linked in via the BINOBJ trick).

All 47 procedures with names, signatures, locals, and source line numbers — e.g. wpisz_wartosci_agros(sesjak, cenanw, cenast, mini, maxi, war, ilo) at line 197, agros_nowses(var cenan1, cenas, min, max, czujnik, ryzyko, sesja, sesjem) at DATA1.PAS:17, the Corupt fake-corruption error handler at line 441, and a ~1,128-line main body holding the whole event loop (F2 Kupno / F3 Sprzedaż are inline, not procedures). Fun fossil: the copy-pasted *_nowses procedures have their first parameter named cenan1 through cenan8.

Your save file decoded — GAME.SAV is the 418-byte rekord type; the save shows session 8, 2,390 zł cash from a 2,000 zł start, no shares held, with full price/min/max/risk state for AGROS, BIG, BPH, BSK, KĘTY, OPTIMUS, WEDEL and ŻYWIEC. GIELDA.CFG is just the 1-byte sound flag.

## Final Result

There they are — your source code is back. The top four are UTF-8 (readable in any modern editor), the DOS/ copies are CP852-encoded byte-for-byte like your originals, so they'll compile in Turbo Pascal 7.0 under DOSBox (instructions in COMPILE.txt — you just need EGAVGA.BGI and SANS.CHR converted with BINOBJ).

A few things you might enjoy rediscovering in your own 12-to-14-year-old code:

The price engine (DATA1) — each session: oile := Round(cenas/10) (moves are ~10% of price), a 1-in-6 ryzyko roll that freezes the price entirely, then the trend czujnik drives the move up/down, with clamps at 50 and 3000. The czujnik = 3 branch literally does cenan := cenan;.

Prognozy (DATA2) — when you press F4 and no prognosis exists yet, there's a 1-in-3 risk chance per attempt that the trend itself re-randomizes and it retries — so asking for a forecast could secretly change the market.

Quirks preserved exactly: F1 (Pomoc) was never implemented — it just redraws the screen. F5 shows "WYKRES W CZASIE PRODUKCJI !!!" plus your free memory via Str(MemAvail, sra) — and yes, the variable really is named sra. The finance-display procedures take integer params but get longints, so amounts past 32767 would have wrapped.

One honest caveat: everything traceable to the binary is faithful — every identifier, type, signature, screen text, key code, the GAME.SAV record layout (agros1..agros12 and friends), even per-line statement order. The only things Borland didn't store were the goto label names, so nowases, odswiez, kupsel etc. are my reconstructions, and exact indentation is approximate.

# Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories — versão nativa para PC

Este projeto transforma o **Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories** (PlayStation 1, versão americana)
em um jogo de **Windows** de verdade, sem emulador. O código do jogo foi decompilado e
recompilado para PC.

> **Importante:** o jogo **não vem junto**. Você precisa ter a sua própria cópia do jogo
> (um arquivo `.bin`). Este repositório só tem o código do programa.

> **Status:** experimental. As mudanças deste projeto (veja
> [O que este projeto muda](#o-que-este-projeto-muda)) ainda estão sendo testadas.

![O campo de duelo em resolução 4x](docs/screenshots/field.jpg)

---

## Do que você precisa

- Um PC com **Windows 10 ou 11 (64 bits)**.
- **Internet na primeira vez** que abrir o jogo (ele baixa sozinho as ferramentas que precisa).
- Cerca de **2 GB livres** no disco.
- O arquivo **`.bin`** do jogo **Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories (USA)** — código **SLUS-01411**.
  - Geralmente ele vem acompanhado de um arquivo `.cue` com o mesmo nome. Só o `.bin` é usado.
  - Versões europeias ou japonesas **não funcionam**.

Você **não** precisa instalar nada antes: nem Python, nem compilador. O próprio programa cuida disso.

---

## Como instalar e jogar (passo a passo)

### 1. Baixe este projeto

No topo desta página do GitHub, clique no botão verde **Code** e depois em **Download ZIP**.

Antes de extrair o ZIP: clique com o botão direito nele, vá em **Propriedades**, marque
**Desbloquear** (se aparecer) e clique em **OK**. Isso evita avisos do Windows mais tarde.

Extraia o ZIP para uma pasta fácil de achar, por exemplo `C:\Jogos\yfm-native`.

> Quem usa Git pode simplesmente rodar
> `git clone https://github.com/Luizhsampaio/yfm-native.git`.

### 2. Coloque o jogo na pasta `game`

Dentro da pasta do projeto, crie uma pasta chamada **`game`** (se ela ainda não existir) e
copie o seu arquivo **`.bin`** para dentro dela. O nome do arquivo não importa.

Deve ficar assim:

```
yfm-native\
   game\
      Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories (USA).bin
   play.bat
   ...
```

### 3. Abra o jogo

Dê **dois cliques em `play.bat`**.

**A primeira vez demora** (de 5 a 15 minutos, dependendo do PC e da internet). Uma janela
preta vai mostrar o progresso. Nessa primeira vez o programa:

1. **Abre o seu `.bin`** e copia os arquivos do jogo para a pasta `game\disc`
   (leva poucos segundos e é feito só uma vez);
2. **Baixa as ferramentas** de que precisa (dentro da pasta `tmp`, sem instalar nada no Windows);
3. **Monta o jogo** para o seu PC;
4. **Abre o jogo.**

**Das próximas vezes**, é só dar dois cliques em `play.bat` de novo — abre em segundos.

### 4. (Opcional) Apague o `.bin`

Depois que o jogo abrir pela primeira vez, a pasta `game` vai ter o arquivo `yfm-disc.txt`
e a pasta `disc`. A partir daí o **`.bin` não é mais necessário** e pode ser apagado
(guarde uma cópia em outro lugar, se quiser).

Não apague nem mexa na pasta `game\disc` nem no `game\yfm-disc.txt`: é deles que o jogo lê.

---

## Controles

Dá para jogar com **teclado** ou **controle** (Xbox e compatíveis). Os controles podem ser
trocados no menu do jogo.

| PlayStation | Teclado | Controle Xbox |
|---|---|---|
| Direcionais | Setas | Direcional ou analógico esquerdo |
| ✕ (Xis) — confirmar | X | A |
| ◯ (Bola) — voltar | S | B |
| ▢ (Quadrado) | Z | X |
| △ (Triângulo) | A | Y |
| L1 / R1 | Q / W | LB / RB |
| L2 / R2 | E / R | LT / RT |
| Start | Enter | Menu/Start |
| Select | Shift direito | View/Back |

**Dica:** para ver a batalha em 3D, escolha o monstro alvo do ataque e confirme com
**Quadrado (tecla Z)** em vez de Xis.

### Menu do programa

Aperte **F10** para abrir a barra de menus. Nela você encontra, entre outras coisas:

- **Video > Resolution > Internal 4x** — gráficos mais nítidos;
- **Video > HD text** — textos em alta resolução;
- **Game > Mods** — ativar e desativar mods;
- **Game > Language** — idioma (os idiomas das versões europeias).

> O jogo pode avisar que existe uma "versão nova". Esse aviso é do **projeto original**
> (veja [Créditos](#créditos-e-licença)), não deste. Para desligar:
> **Help > Check for updates at start**.

---

## Saves (jogo salvo)

Os saves ficam em **`Documentos\My Games\YFM Re-Decomp\saves`**.

**Trazer o save de um emulador:** copie o arquivo de cartão de memória do emulador
(`.mcr`, `.mcd`, `.srm`, `.gme`, `.mcs`, `.psv`...) para essa pasta `saves`. Depois escolha
**LOAD** na tela inicial. (No DuckStation e no ePSXe esses arquivos ficam na pasta `memcards`.)
"Save states" de emulador não servem: salve dentro do jogo antes.

---

## Problemas comuns

**"O Windows protegeu o computador" (tela azul do SmartScreen)**
Clique em **Mais informações** e depois em **Executar assim mesmo**. Isso acontece porque o
programa é montado no seu PC e não tem assinatura digital.

**O antivírus bloqueia o jogo / "Acesso negado"**
Alguns antivírus (principalmente em computadores de empresa) bloqueiam programas recém-criados.
Em PC pessoal, adicione a pasta do projeto como exceção no antivírus. Em PC de empresa, fale
com o suporte de TI ou use outro computador.

**"Put your disc image in the game folder first"**
O programa não achou o jogo. Confira se:
- a pasta se chama exatamente `game` e está **dentro** da pasta do projeto (ao lado do `play.bat`);
- o arquivo dentro dela é o **`.bin`** (não o `.cue`).

**"this is not the Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories (USA, SLUS-01411) disc"**
O `.bin` não é da versão americana do jogo. Só a versão USA (SLUS-01411) funciona.

**A janela preta mostra um erro e o jogo não abre**
- Na primeira vez, confira se o PC está conectado à internet e rode o `play.bat` de novo.
- Se o erro continuar, a janela mostra onde ficou o relatório do problema (pasta `tmp\pc`,
  arquivos `crash-...txt` e `last-session.log`). Abra uma *issue* aqui no GitHub e anexe esses arquivos.

**Quero atualizar o projeto**
Baixe o ZIP novo (ou rode `git pull`) e **copie a sua pasta `game` antiga para dentro dele**.
A pasta `game` nunca é substituída pela atualização.

---

## Avisos importantes

- **Não envie a pasta `game` para o GitHub nem compartilhe os arquivos do jogo.** Eles são
  da Konami. O projeto já está configurado para o Git ignorar essa pasta (arquivo `.gitignore`);
  não apague esse arquivo.
- Cada pessoa deve usar a sua própria cópia do jogo.

---

## O que este projeto muda

Este repositório parte do
[Yu-Gi-Oh! Forbidden Memories Recompiled](https://github.com/Unchiga/Yu-Gi-Oh-Forbidden-Memories-Recompiled)
e tem o objetivo de deixar o jogo **100% nativo**:

- **Animações de ataque dos monstros em código nativo.** No projeto original, as animações de
  ataque de cada monstro (código do PlayStation guardado no arquivo `MODEL.MRG`) rodavam num
  "mini emulador" embutido. Aqui elas são traduzidas automaticamente para C durante a montagem
  do jogo (`tools/pc/model_recomp.py`).
- **O jogo roda a partir de arquivos abertos, sem o `.bin`.** O `.bin` é aberto uma única vez
  e os arquivos do jogo vão para `game\disc` (`tools/pc/extract_disc.py`). Depois disso o `.bin`
  pode ser apagado.

Próximos passos planejados: converter os arquivos do jogo para formatos comuns (imagens PNG,
áudio, vídeo) e remover a dependência do mapa de memória do PlayStation.

---

## Para desenvolvedores

- Como o jogo é montado: [notes/pc-build.md](notes/pc-build.md)
  (inclui a seção sobre o disco extraído).
- Mods: [notes/modding.md](notes/modding.md) · FM Editor: [tools/pc/fm_editor/README.md](tools/pc/fm_editor/README.md)
- Comparar as animações traduzidas com o interpretador original:
  `python tools\pc\test_model_recomp.py`
- Decompilação: todas as funções do jogo batem byte a byte com o original
  (`make tools` e `make match`; veja [notes/setup.md](notes/setup.md)).

# HS/Link (32-bit)

A modern **32-bit native port** of the HS/Link bidirectional
file-transfer protocol — Samuel H. Smith's early-1990s BBS protocol
that did simultaneous two-way transfer with in-band chat over a single
connection.

![HSLink-Modern Bidirectional File Transfer](./assets/screenshots/hslink1.png)

![HSLink-Modern Chat Session](./assets/screenshots/hslink2.png)


The goal: make HS/Link useful again to sysops running modern
(telnet/TCP) BBS systems, by porting it from 16-bit DOS / FOSSIL to a
modern program that connects over **TCP** — while preserving the wire
format exactly, so it interoperates with existing HS/Link installations.

It is built as **one portable codebase** that compiles to **x86
(32-bit Windows)**, **x64 (64-bit Windows)**, and **Linux**. 32-bit
Windows is the first build to prove (it's what sysops expect today and
pairs with the live test peer); 64-bit ensures the protocol outlives
32-bit environments as they age out.

This is a standalone project. It is **not** another 16-bit DOS build
(one already exists and runs fine); the recovered 16-bit source is the
specification and starting material for the modern port.

## Status

Early scaffolding. The repository holds:

  - the analysis and specifications produced from the recovered source
    (`docs/`),
  - the recovered original source itself, as reference/specification
    material (`reference/`), and
  - a **buildable skeleton** (`src/`) — a Visual Studio 2022 solution
    (x86 + x64) that compiles and runs, with the `Com*` transport
    interface stubbed out, ready for the protocol engine to be brought
    in and modernized.

No protocol logic is implemented yet; see `docs/technical-assessment.md`
for the roadmap and `src/README.md` for how to build the skeleton.

## Documentation

| Doc | What it covers |
|-----|----------------|
| `docs/saga.md` | History of HS/Link, the 1996 recovery, and the legal basis for this project |
| `docs/technical-assessment.md` | Code analysis of the recovered source, architecture, what ports vs. what's discarded, and the roadmap |
| `docs/protocol-spec.md` | The packet-level wire format — the **interop contract** the port must match byte-for-byte |
| `docs/com-api.md` | The ~20-function transport boundary to implement over a socket |
| `docs/build-and-test.md` | Toolchain (VS 2022, x86, portable sockets) and how to test against a live HS/Link peer |
| `docs/provenance/` | The original author's release notes (verbatim) and project attribution |

## The short version of the plan

1. Bring the recovered protocol engine (the "HDK": `HSRECV.C`,
   `HSTRANS.C`, `HSTOP.C`, `HSPRIV.H`) and application layer into a
   32-bit project; clean out the DOS-isms until it compiles.
2. Implement the `Com*` transport interface over a portable socket
   layer (Winsock / BSD sockets) with telnet (IAC) handling.
3. Implement the host-integration stubs against the local filesystem and
   a console/log UI.
4. Conformance-test against a live 16-bit HS/Link peer (the existing
   protocol is the test oracle); debug wire-format mismatches against
   the real thing.
5. Validate the Linux build; harden timeouts, resume, and chat.

## Provenance, briefly

HS/Link's source survives because, after a 1995 burglary cost Samuel H.
Smith his development system and backups, he released what he could
recover in August 1996 as free, unsupported software — explicitly hoping
others would "keep the protocol alive, at least in some changed form."
This project is that changed form. See `docs/saga.md`.

# SimGolf in the browser

A fan port of **Sid Meier's SimGolf** (Firaxis / EA, 2002) to WebAssembly, so
it runs in a web browser on Mac, Linux and Windows with nothing to install.

**Play: https://richardatct.github.io/simgolf-web/**

This repository and the page contain no game files. You bring your own copy of
the game, and it never leaves your computer.

## How to play

1. Get the game files. You need two things:
   - the **game disc**: the `.7z` from the
     [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/sid-meiers-sim-golf-1641547)
     (about 250 MB; an `.iso` of the disc from elsewhere works too), and
   - the **v1.02 no-CD `golf.exe`**, usually a zip called
     `SIMGOLF.102.ENG.MYTH.NOCD.ZIP`, from
     [Abandonware DOS](https://www.abandonwaredos.com/abandonware-game.php?abandonware=Sid+Meier%27s+SimGolf&gid=2317).
2. Open the page in **Chrome or Edge, version 137 or newer**, on a desktop or
   laptop. (Firefox and Safari can't run it yet.)
3. Click **Choose your game files** and pick both files as they downloaded;
   there's no need to unzip anything. The page unpacks the game in about a
   minute and starts it. Next time it goes straight to the game.

## Good to know

- Saves stay in your browser. Press **Alt+S** (**Option+S** on a Mac) in the
  game, or click the Saves button in the bottom-right corner, to download a
  save or import one. Ctrl+F8 also works except on a Mac, where macOS keeps it.
- To start over with different files, press **Alt+S** and use the button at
  the bottom of the panel.
- To turn off scrolling the course by touching a screen edge with the
  pointer, press **Alt+S** and untick it under Settings (or add
  `?edgescroll=0` to the address). The arrow keys still scroll.
- Clearing your browser's site data for the page removes the unpacked game
  and your saves (download the saves first).

## Support

If you're enjoying SimGolf again, you can
[buy me a coffee](https://donate.stripe.com/eVq6oG1U46TL3ut28h9R600). Thank you!

## How it works

The game isn't emulated. Its code was decompiled with Ghidra and translated
mechanically into C, which Emscripten compiles to WebAssembly. Windows,
graphics, the 3D terrain renderer and sound are replaced with browser
implementations. [docs/porting.md](docs/porting.md) explains the approach and
[docs/building.md](docs/building.md) how to build it yourself.

The same code also runs as a desktop app for macOS and Windows: the
WebAssembly module is translated back to native code with wasm2c and runs in
a small SDL2 host ([native/README.md](native/README.md)).

## Legal

This is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by
Firaxis Games, Electronic Arts or Take-Two Interactive. SimGolf and its
assets are their property; this project distributes none of the game's files.
The port's own code is MIT licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party pieces
keep their licences (`third_party/`: unshield and webm-muxer are MIT, 7-Zip and FFmpeg are LGPL).

# OVERKILL Runtime & Evidence-Driven Source Port

> A custom 8086/DOS runtime and reverse-engineering framework for rebuilding
> **OVERKILL: The Six-Planet Mega Blast** from the original executable outward.

This project is not trying to write a new game that merely looks like OVERKILL.
It runs the original 16-bit DOS program, treats the binary as the behavioral
oracle, and gradually replaces proven ASM routines with verified Python code.
Over time, those verified routines are promoted upward into recovered,
source-like game systems that can become the basis of a native source port.

```text
original OVERKILL binary
        ↓
custom 8086 + DOS runtime
        ↓
interpreted ASM oracle traces
        ↓
verified CS:IP Python hooks
        ↓
recovered views/adapters/domain/systems
        ↓
future native source-port core
```

The important rule is simple:

> Do not invent the source port. Let it crystallize from verified evidence.

---

## What makes this project interesting?

- It is a **runtime built for one specific DOS game**, not a general emulator.
- The original executable remains runnable and comparable at every step.
- Each lifted hook can be verified against interpreted original ASM.
- Gameplay logic is being moved upward gradually, not rewritten top-down.
- The project now has a clean split between:
  - low-level VM/runtime code,
  - address-facing hooks,
  - DOS-memory views and adapters,
  - pure recovered gameplay/domain systems.

This means the repo is both a reverse-engineering tool and the beginning of a
source-port scaffold.

---

## Start here

| I want to... | Read / run |
| --- | --- |
| Understand the project goal / vision | `docs/overkill/game_recovery_lifecycle.md` (the lifecycle + the canonical doc map) |
| Know what to do next / run the loop | `docs/overkill/overnight_endgame_execution.md` (the one canonical `/goal` brief) |
| See the latest known state | `docs/overkill/run_status.md` |
| Work as an AI agent | `AGENTS.md` |
| Understand the method | `docs/overkill/source_port_methodology.md` |
| Understand the target architecture | `docs/overkill/semantic_crystallization_plan.md` |
| See recovered source-layer rules | `docs/overkill/recovered_source_layer.md` |
| Check current address knowledge | `symbols.json` and `docs/overkill/island_truth_tables.md` |
| Run fast non-viewer tests | `python scripts/run_tests.py --scope dos-re` |
| Play / verify the game | `python scripts/play.py --video tandy --sound adlib` |

---

## Current direction

The project is moving through two connected migrations:

1. **ASM → verified hooks**
   - Unknown original code still runs through the interpreter.
   - Understood routines become exact `CS:IP` hooks.
   - Hook output is compared against original ASM state: registers, flags,
     memory, stack, files, ports, and continuations.

2. **Verified hooks → recovered source layer**
   - Stable hook logic moves out of address-shaped code.
   - DOS state is projected through views/adapters.
   - Pure gameplay decisions live in `overkill/recovered/domain` and
     `overkill/recovered/systems`.
   - Those pure layers must not depend on `cpu`, `mem`, registers, flags,
     segment offsets, or verifier continuations.

The current crystallization target is deliberately conservative: object slots,
collision primitives, coordinate helpers, HUD/status composition, renderer
commands, and other structures that multiple verified routines already point to.

---

## Repository map

```text
dos_re/                     git submodule: reusable narrow DOS reverse-
                            engineering runtime (github.com/missingno7/dos_re).
                            Clone with --recurse-submodules. The package itself
                            is one level deeper, dos_re/dos_re/ -- also carries
                            its own pynuked_opl3/ submodule (optional AdLib PCM):
  cpu.py                    dependency-free 8086 interpreter core
  memory.py                 20-bit real-mode memory model
  dos.py                    narrow DOS/BIOS/port services
  hooks.py                  generic replacement hook registry
  runtime.py                generic DOS-program runtime wiring
  snapshot.py               memory/state snapshot helpers
  verification.py           reusable differential hook verifier
  frame_verify.py           reusable frame comparison engine

overkill/                   OVERKILL-specific game/runtime layer
  hooks.py                  exact CS:IP hook registration surface
  runtime.py                canonical launch/snapshot wiring
  cli.py                    command-line helpers built on dos_re
  verification.py           hook verifier stop metadata and game adapters
  coverage.py               island classifier and coverage summaries
  gameplay/                 lifted gameplay helpers still close to ASM shape
  rendering/                startup graphics, sprites, Tandy/CGA/EGA primitives
  sounds/                   timer, PC speaker, AdLib/YM3812 driver behavior
  asset_codecs/             checksum, packed streams, RLE/LZ, asset tables
  file_io/                  overlay/container file orchestration
  recovered/                source-port crystallization layer
    views/                  DOS-memory overlays; may know offsets/segments
    adapters/               CPU/memory projection and ASM flag/register glue
    domain/                 pure copied source-like records
    systems/                pure gameplay/system functions

docs/                       documentation map, methodology, findings, status
scripts/                    runners, audits, cleanups, profiling, viewer tools
assets/                     local user-supplied original game files; gitignored
artifacts/                  snapshots, traces, caches, verifier evidence
tests/                      CPU/runtime/hook/recovered-layer regression tests
symbols.json                known addresses, names, hypotheses, statuses
AGENTS.md                   durable guardrails for AI agents and humans
```

`dos_re` must stay game-independent. Anything that knows OVERKILL addresses,
assets, hooks, islands, command-tail behavior, or game-specific frame semantics
belongs under `overkill`.

---

## Recovered source-port layers

The recovered layer exists so the upper game logic can eventually run without the
DOS VM.

```text
hooks        exact original address/continuation wrappers
adapters     project DOS memory/register state into source-like data
views        typed overlays over original memory structures
records      pure copied data structures
systems      pure gameplay decisions
```

Current package boundary:

```text
overkill/recovered/views/       may know original offsets, segments, memory layout
overkill/recovered/adapters/    may know CPU/memory and preserve ASM-visible effects
overkill/recovered/domain/      must be pure; no CPU, memory, hooks, offsets
overkill/recovered/systems/     must be pure; no CPU, memory, hooks, offsets
```

Enforce this with:

```bash
python scripts/audit_recovered_layers.py
python scripts/lint.py
```

The intended shape of a lifted routine is:

```text
hook wrapper
  → adapter reads DOS state
  → pure recovered system makes the gameplay decision
  → adapter writes ASM-compatible registers/flags/memory
  → hook returns to the verified continuation
```

This prevents duplicated gameplay logic while still preserving exact original
behavior.

---

## Quick start

`dos_re` is a git submodule, not vendored code -- clone with `--recurse-submodules`,
or run `git submodule update --init --recursive` afterwards.

### 1. Install the project

```bash
python -m pip install -e dos_re/   # the framework -- makes standalone scripts/probes work
python -m pip install -e .
```

For the SDL viewer:

```bash
python -m pip install -e .[viewer]
```

For audible AdLib/FM output:

```bash
python -m pip install -e dos_re/   # makes both dos_re and pynuked_opl3 importable
python -m pip install -e .[adlib]  # cffi, for building the extension below
python -m pynuked_opl3._ffi_build
```

Without the compiled AdLib backend, the VM can still model detection and YM3812
register writes, but the SDL frontend remains silent. Use `--adlib-audio off` if
you want to run the original AdLib path without PCM output.

### 2. Add original game files

This repository does **not** ship the original game data.

Place your local copy under `assets/`, for example:

```text
assets/OVERKILL
assets/OVERKILL.EXE
```

The canonical source inputs are the original files. Generated convenience files
such as unpacked executables or overlay blobs must be treated as build/evidence
artifacts, not source assets.

### 3. Run fast checks

```bash
python scripts/run_tests.py --scope dos-re
python scripts/lint.py
```

### 4. Launch the game

```bash
python scripts/play.py --video tandy --sound adlib
```

Other useful variants:

```bash
python scripts/play.py --video tandy
python scripts/play.py --video ega
python scripts/play.py --video cga
python scripts/play.py --snapshot artifacts/evidence/<snapshot-dir>
```

---

## Verification workflow

Every replacement is a proof obligation.

```text
observe
  → classify
  → choose boundary
  → build ASM oracle
  → implement hook
  → verify
  → document
  → move upward when stable
```

For a focused hook:

```bash
python scripts/play.py --verify-hook 1010:ECF2 --verify-stop-on-diff
```

For broad live verification:

```bash
python scripts/play.py --verify-hooks --verify-require-metadata
```

For previewing while verifying:

```bash
python scripts/play.py \
  --demo artifacts/demos/<demo-name> \
  --verify-hooks \
  --verify-preview \
  --sound adlib
```

For frame-level verification:

```bash
python scripts/play.py --snapshot artifacts/evidence/<snapshot-dir> --verify-frames
```

For current island closure signals:

```bash
python scripts/audit_islands.py --all-hooks
```

`closed-candidate` means no known script-detected blockers; it is a useful
signal, not a substitute for oracle evidence.

---

## Repro artifacts and debugging

The runtime can preserve hard-to-reach failures.

When replaying a long demo, hook divergence can create a shorter suffix/repro
demo under:

```text
artifacts/repros/
```

Hook-verifier divergence repros are captured from the verifier's **pre-hook**
clone whenever possible, not from the already-mutated live runtime after the
mismatch.  Frame-verifier divergence repros similarly save the candidate runtime
before the first divergent frame.  Check `input_demo.json`/`repro.json` metadata
for `repro_state` values such as `pre_hook` or
`candidate_pre_divergent_frame`.

Interactive crashes can also save a crash snapshot with enough VM state to retry
from the failure point:

```bash
python scripts/play.py --snapshot artifacts/repros/<crash-dir> --video tandy --sound adlib
```

Typical snapshot contents:

```text
memory_1mb.bin
state.json
trace_tail.txt
repro.json        # for repro/crash artifacts when available
```

---

## Runtime world / level-editor probes

These commands help turn live verified snapshots into source-like evidence for
future level editor and source-port work:

```text
python scripts/dump_world.py --demo artifacts/demos/demo_play_tandy_20260616_000527 \
  --active-only --summary -o artifacts/world_dump_demo_20260616_000527_start.json

python scripts/trace_world_writes.py --demo artifacts/demos/demo_play_tandy_20260616_000527 \
  --max-steps 20000 --max-events 2000 \
  -o artifacts/world_write_trace_demo_20260616_000527_enriched_20000.json

python scripts/summarize_world_writes.py \
  artifacts/world_write_trace_demo_20260616_000527_enriched_20000.json \
  -o artifacts/world_write_summary_demo_20260616_000527_enriched_20000.json --text
```

`dump_world.py` projects recovered object/effect slots, pointer tables, boss
group pointers, and important globals into JSON.  `trace_world_writes.py` traces
writes to those regions and decorates each event with writer island/symbol plus
a decoded target such as `effect_contact_slots_23b4[3].logic_id`.
`summarize_world_writes.py` groups those events by writer and field so
materialisation/setup routines can be found from evidence instead of guessed.

## Useful commands

Inspect the executable:

```bash
python -m overkill.cli info assets/OVERKILL
```

Run a short trace:

```bash
python -m overkill.cli trace assets/OVERKILL \
  --game-root assets \
  --steps 5000 \
  --out trace_start.txt
```

Create a snapshot:

```bash
python -m overkill.cli snapshot assets/OVERKILL \
  --game-root assets \
  --steps 100000 \
  --trace-tail 128 \
  --out-dir artifacts/evidence/snapshot_after_bootstrap_100k
```

Render a saved frame without SDL:

```bash
python scripts/render_frame.py \
  artifacts/evidence/<snapshot-dir> \
  --video tandy \
  --out frame.png
```

Profile interpreted hotspots:

```bash
python scripts/profile_hotspots.py 2000000
```

Clean generated local outputs:

```bash
python scripts/clean.py
python scripts/clean.py --artifacts
```

---

## Bootstrap/static-runtime boundary

The project treats the original startup path as an oracle/extraction layer, not
as the final source-port architecture.

Write the current bootstrap boundary manifest:

```bash
python -m overkill.cli bootstrap-boundary \
  --video tandy \
  --sound adlib \
  --out artifacts/static_runtime_boundary.json
```

Materialize an initialized runtime bundle from the original files:

```bash
python -m overkill.cli static-runtime-bundle assets/OVERKILL \
  --game-root assets \
  --video tandy \
  --sound adlib \
  --out-dir artifacts/static_runtime_bundle
```

See `docs/overkill/bootstrap_static_boundary.md`,
`overkill/bootstrap_boundary.py`, and `overkill/static_runtime_bundle.py`.

---

## Documentation map

| Document | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | Durable workflow and guardrails for AI agents/humans |
| `docs/README.md` | Full documentation index |
| `docs/overkill/run_status.md` | Current checkpoint, recent validations, next work |
| `docs/overkill/semantic_crystallization_plan.md` | Main plan for lifting verified behavior into recovered source layers |
| `docs/overkill/recovered_source_layer.md` | Current `views/adapters/domain/systems` split |
| `docs/overkill/source_port_methodology.md` | OVERKILL-specific source-port playbook |
| `docs/dos_re/source_port_methodology.md` | Reusable DOS RE methodology |
| `docs/overkill/runtime_findings.md` | Accumulated reverse-engineering findings |
| `docs/overkill/island_truth_tables.md` | Per-island evidence, confidence, guesses, frontiers |
| `docs/architecture/package_boundary.md` | Package ownership and dependency rules |
| `docs/architecture/third_party.md` | Vendored third-party policy |
| `symbols.json` | Address labels, hypotheses, hook status |

Prefer explicit segment:offset notation such as `1010:95C9` when documenting
original code.

---

## Development rules

- Fidelity first, readability second, meaning third.
- Do not add high-level gameplay names without evidence.
- Do not duplicate gameplay decisions across hooks and recovered systems.
- Keep `overkill/hooks.py` as a thin address-facing wrapper layer.
- Promote stable behavior upward only when the core decision can be expressed
  without CPU/memory/register/flag dependencies.
- Keep `dos_re` independent of OVERKILL.
- Run verifier, audit, and focused tests after behavioral changes.
- Keep durable policy in docs; keep time-sensitive status in
  `docs/overkill/run_status.md`.

This project should get cleaner because evidence converges, not because a model
was guessed early.

Recreation and analysis of the physics engine from the classic racing game from 1995.

* No assets required;
